editorial.headline: Counting Cargo, With a Bali Ownership Limit
editorial.standfirst: Independent tally work records the facts of cargo movement for owners and carriers—open nationally to full foreign ownership, but limited in Bali to a 49% foreign stake.
editorial.body:
Independent tally activity is the discipline of establishing the facts around cargo: counting it, measuring it, weighing it and making the corresponding records for the cargo owner and/or carrier. The scope expressly includes independent tally operations at ports. It is therefore a defined cargo-recording service, built around a clear account of the load rather than a generic label for commercial activity.

The registration record is open to businesses at Micro, Small, Medium and Large scale. That breadth matters because the activity is not reserved in the record for one class of enterprise. Whether the work is organised on a smaller footing or at a larger operating scale, the stated scope remains the same: measurement, count, weight and documentation concerning cargo for those with an interest in it.

Nationally, the position is open. The foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, which means the national record permits foreign ownership up to full ownership. Bali gives the activity a different contour. Its status is TERBATAS: restricted. Within the Bali entry’s cargo/freight-forwarding context, foreign nationals may hold no more than 49%. National openness does not transplant unchanged to Bali; the island listing carries a 49% ceiling for foreign nationals.

The record also notes a permanent, island-wide Bali rule that blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. This activity’s own Bali entry is not marked as blocked; it is marked TERBATAS and states the 49% foreign-ownership limit. The slim record does not assign this activity a risk classification, so the precise reading is to keep those two facts distinct: the general moratorium applies to the risk categories named in the rule, while this activity’s recorded Bali treatment is a restriction on foreign ownership. For founders, that distinction is the essential one: a 100% national ceiling is not the Bali position for this activity.
